items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to requiring
property owners and lessors of certain properties that have been vacated to
inspect such property for abandoned animals
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1784

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to requir-
ing property owners and lessors of certain properties that have been
vacated to inspect such property for abandoned animals

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this legislation is to require landlords to inspect
vacated properties to ensure no animals were left abandoned.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Section 373 of the Agriculture and Markets Law is amended by
a new subdivision 2-a.

Section 2: Effective Date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Often times when people are forced from their homes it is due to finan-
cial reasons or a change in lifestyle or re-location. These types of
reasons for vacating a home can occasionally lead individuals to make
hasty and desperate decisions for their pets.  These types of decisions
can also have profound and sometime lethal consequences for their aban-
doned pets.

This legislation would require owners of real property to inspect
vacated properties to check to see that no animals were left abandoned
in the home. The bill would require the landowner to notify animal
control, police or SPCA in order for the animal to be removed or cared
for until such time as it can be removed. The legislation also clarifies
that the landlord is not deemed the owner of such animal and failure to
check for abandon pets will result in a fine to he paid into the animal
population control fund. Massachusetts passed a similar law in 2018.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S7119 Agriculture / A8841 agriculture

2021-2022: S4081-A Agriculture; Passed Senate

2023: S6365 (passed Senate) / A2881 (Agriculture Committee)

2024: S6365 (passed Senate) / A2881 (Agriculture Committee)

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

This legislation will have no local fiscal implications; any fines
collected will be deposited into the State's Animal population control
fund.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the real property actions and proceedings law, in relation to
requiring property owners of certain properties that have been vacated or
abandoned to inspect such property for abandoned companion animals
A.lawSection: Real Property Actions and Proceedings Law
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1784A

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property actions and proceedings law, in
relation to requiring property owners of certain properties that have
been vacated or abandoned to inspect such property for abandoned compan-
ion animals

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this legislation is to require property owners to inspect
vacated and abandoned properties for the presence of abandoned companion
animals.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Paragraph c of subdivision 2 of section 1307 of real property
actions and proceedings law is amended and new paragraphs e and f are
added to subdivision 2.

Section 2: Section 1971 of the real property actions and proceedings law
is amended by adding a new subdivision 3.

Section 3: Effective Date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

The A-print no longer amends the Agriculture and Markets Law; it instead
amends the Real Property Actions and Proceedings Law. The A-print
provides that a plaintiff, property owner, who commences a mortgage
foreclosure action must inspect a vacated or abandoned residential prop-
erty for abandoned companion animals. If the property owner fails to
conduct this inspection, the owner will be found in violation of this
section and subject to a civil penalty. If an abandoned companion animal
is found, the property owner must notify a dog control officer, the
police, or an agent or officer of a duly incorporated humane society.or
duly incorporated society for the prevention of cruelty to animals. The
department or agency of a city, town or village responsible for the
enforcement of multiple dwelling law, multiple residence law, or the
occupancy and maintenance of residential property, would also be
required to conduct an inspection for abandoned companion animals if it
finds a dwelling to be abandoned.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

When people are forced from their homes it is typically due an emergency
that greatly upends the lives of the family or individual.  The sudden
need to vacate a home can occasionally led individuals to make hasty and
desperate decisions for their pets. These decisions can have profound
and lethal consequences for their abandoned pets.

This legislation would require owners of real property to inspect
vacated properties within three days to check to see that no animals
were left abandoned in the home. The bill would require the landowner to
notify animal control, police or SPCA for the animal to be removed or
cared for until such time as it can be removed. The legislation also
clarifies that the landlord is not deemed the owner of such animal and
failure to check for abandon pets will result in a fine to be paid into
the animal population control fund.  Massachusetts passed a similar law
in 2018.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Formerly A-8841 of 2020, died in Agriculture Committee.

Formerly A-1769 of 2022, died in Agriculture Committee.

Formerly A-2881 of 2023, died in Agriculture Committee.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

This legislation will have no local fiscal implications; any fines
collected will be deposited into the State's animal population control
fund.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Provides for the inspection of property that has been vacated or abandoned for abandoned companion animals.
title: Relates to the inspection of certain vacated or abandoned properties for abandoned companion animals
